findings.message: The criteria cannot all be met. This ticket depends on storm-ledger, so squatch/storm.py and tests/test_storm.py already exist on main when it runs. Both storm seeds fence those paths, so the criterion 'pins every existing fence path as existing Context' requires them in Context. Scope in says the opposite: keep them outside Context because they are 'sibling-new', and tests/test_storm.py 'is not Context because it is sibling-new at authoring time'. They are not siblings in this admission. storm-ledger was admitted by phase3-continue-15 and is this ticket's dependency. Section 20 says later seeds authored after a sibling merges include the then-existing surfaces in their Context.
findings.paved_road: Treat squatch/storm.py and tests/test_storm.py as existing paths that storm-ledger owns. Add them to the storm seeds' Context: tests/test_storm.py for both seeds, since it is fenced in both; squatch/storm.py wherever headroom allows. Anything that does not fit headroom becomes an explicit fenced on-demand exception with its own size pin, following the kill-cli-activation partition. Drop the 'no on-demand exceptions' wording if you use one. Restrict the 'no sibling-new paths in Context' rule to paths this admission creates: tests/test_storm_producer.py, tests/test_storm_notification_activation.py and tests/test_seeded_phase3_17.py.

findings.message: The storm-notification-activation fence is squatch/storm.py, squatch/box.py, squatch/daemon.py and two tests. It cannot prove 'the real in-process production composition'. In the shown Context, daemon.py only defines dormant compose_* hooks. The production composition is exercised through squatch.__main__ (_locked, _control_factory, _pipeline), and every earlier activation fenced __main__.py (or drain.py) to bind its hook. With this fence the activation can only compose storm in daemon.py, which is dormant construction, not activation.
findings.paved_road: Fence squatch/__main__.py (and squatch/drain.py if the bootstrap drain is the activated path) in storm-notification-activation's hooks, as an on-demand exception if headroom requires it. Pin that fence and its Context/on-demand classification in tests/test_seeded_phase3_16.py. Alternatively, state concretely which existing production caller in daemon.py already reaches storm composition without an edit outside the fence.

findings.message: Phase 3 seeds may cite only section 20, and section 20 says its compact registry incorporates the section 12 laws. For storm-ledger, though, the registry gives only files and a dependency ('`journal-roll`, then `storm-ledger` (`squatch/journal.py`, `squatch/storm.py`, ...)'). It never says what a storm occurrence is, what identity or signature it is keyed by, its journal event type, key and body shape, any window or threshold, how it folds across rolled segments (the reason it depends on `journal-roll`), or what 'dormant' allows reaching it. Flake detection and flake release have exactly this contract in their own clarification paragraph (signal key `flake/<box_id>`, body `{kind: flake_detected, ...}`, fold and idempotence rules); storm has none. Without it, the author cannot write criteria an implementer can verify, and the later `storm-producer-wiring`, `storm-notification-activation` and `storm-dispatch-hold` seeds would inherit whatever shape the implementer guessed.
findings.paved_road: fix the plan, then re-author the ticket

findings.message: The criterion 'directly proves the dormant occurrence-ledger boundary' names no observable behavior (no event, key, body, fold result or trip condition). The criterion 'proves no producer wiring, notification activation, or dispatch hold is implemented or activated' names no mechanism (such as an AST import-closure check or the absence of a composition hook). Neither can be checked by a script, so review cannot tell a correct implementation from an arbitrary one.
